maya: Heads up — I ran a quick perf pass on the new AWQ weight-only path and I'm seeing a puzzling 8-12% tail latency bump on medium-length chats (avg seq 160).

jgonz: hmm, same cluster as the nightly? which kernel variant?

maya: nightly image gcr/redwood-infer:3.2.1-awq, kernel selector picked `int8_wt_pack_deconv` for many layers instead of `int8_wt_pack_stream`. I think the deconv path increases unpack ops per KV hit.

riley: "deconv" path? I thought deconv was our internal name for the unpack+reorder microkernel when group_size < 32. Are you using small groups?

maya: Yep — AWQ calibration pushed group_size=16 for better quality on the LLM-embed workload. We calibrated for accuracy but didn't recheck perf for mid-length chats.

jgonz: can you paste the perf counters? nvprof / nsight summary?

maya: pasted perf snippet: ```
# nvprof summary (short)
GPU time: 1.23 ms  (pack_stream)
GPU time: 1.67 ms  (pack_deconv)
SM occupancy pack_stream 68% -> pack_deconv 52%
L2 hit rate pack_stream 88% -> pack_deconv 81%
DRAM bw up 14% on deconv
```

riley: that matches more memory traffic and lower occupancy — deconv has a scatter/gather-like pattern that kills coalescing. If group_size=16 then we do more index math per warp.

maya: hypothesis: smaller groups -> more frequent pack/unpack boundary ops -> worse prefetch behavior for KV cache. KV cache hotpath perf shows extra stalls when pack_deconv chosen.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled canary aws-spot-ml-06 -> 3.2.1-awq (subset: 5 hosts), monitoring enabled

jgonz: did you try forcing kernel selection to pack_stream to confirm regression?

maya: quick test forcing selector to prefer stream: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFER=pack_stream` on canary. Latency dropped back to baseline for same traffic pattern. So selector choice is causal.

riley: OK, two knobs: 1) make selector prefer stream when seq in [64,256] and group_size<=32; 2) change AWQ calibration to bias group_size>=32 for production prompts where perf matters. But we need microbench numbers for quality vs speed tradeoff.

devan: also check batching heuristics — our continuous batcher groups requests by prefix length; if next-token traffic has varied prefixes we might create batches that amplify deconv penalties. Could be an interaction between our batcher and kernel selector.

maya: good point — when I replayed production traces the median batch had a 30% variance in sequence length. The selector currently uses max_seq to pick kernel, which pushes deconv if a single short sequence is present.

jgonz: we should change selector to use a percentile like p95_seq in batch rather than max_seq. That will avoid the outlier short seq forcing deconv for whole batch.

riley: I'd add a small heuristic: if p95_seq <= 64 use stream; if p95_seq between 64-256 prefer stream unless group_size<24 and model layer is depthwise-heavy. Can we land this as quick patch?

maya: I'll prototype selector change and run offline replay. I have two replays: one with 10k chats (traffic A) and one with 25k mixed (traffic B). Preliminary results: p95-based selector reduces deconv usage by 82% and lowers p99 tail by ~9% on traffic A.

devan: also please capture KV cache telemetry — number of KV hits that triggered unpack, and per-request extra memcpy time. We need concrete counters for eng-runtime dashboard.

maya: noted. I'll add counters: `kv_unwrap_ms`, `kernel_switch_count`, `pack_bytes_read` to the runtime.

ops-bot: perf-scan-bot: created issue #4567 "pack_deconv tail on 3.2.1-awq" and attached logs

jgonz: unrelated note — how does GPTQ path compare? We saw earlier that GPTQ with group_size 64 had slightly worse RMSE but much better throughput because it avoids deconv. Worth rerunning a quality vs perf sweep comparing AWQ(g16/32) vs GPTQ(g64).

riley: agree. Let's run a grid: AWQ g=16,32,64; GPTQ g=32,64; measure perplexity delta on eval set + p50/p95/p99 latency under replayed load. Also capture GPU util and L2 miss.

maya: scheduling those now. ETA for first sweep: ~6 hours on canary pool (low priority). If results are clear, will propose making default AWQ cal target group_size>=32 for production models.

devan: one caveat — some customers need the AWQ g=16 quality delta. We should implement model-variant routing: prefer g=32 quantized model for hosted tier, but allow g=16 variant behind a flag for customers who need the extra quality. That avoids a blanket change.

jgonz: +1. Also add a runtime fallback: if kernel selector sees pack_deconv chosen for >40% of layers and observed p99 increases >5% vs baseline, auto-fallback to pack_stream and emit alert. That will reduce live regressions.

maya: will prototype fallback logic in selector and add metrics. I'll post results in this thread when sweeps finish.

riley: thanks — appreciate the sleuthing. Small followups: attach nvprof flame for a representative request and a small script to reproduce with `infer-bench --seq=160 --group=16 --model=awq`.

maya: attaching artifact links (private): `s3://redwood-perf/3498765432/trace.nvprof`, `s3://redwood-perf/3498765432/replay.tar.gz`.

ops-bot: monitor-bot: canary p99 latency alert cleared after REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFER flip on canary hosts

jgonz: nice. When you have the grid results, let's decide defaults and roll plan. Thanks maya + team :thumbsup:
